text: The paper reports that with 6 pixels, debate with precommit turns a 59.4% accurate judge into an 88.9% accurate debate in which the judge wins on 88.9% of the images in the MNIST test set, and with 4 pixels a 48.2% accurate judge becomes an 85.2% accurate debate. The authors state precommit is crucial for both pixel budgets because the liar does much better when the lie can adapt in different parts of the game tree; without the mean-over-3-seeds adjustment the honest player wins 87.7% (6 pixels) and 83.8% (4 pixels).
title: MNIST debate with precommit: judge accuracy 59.4% to 88.9% (6 px), 48.2% to 85.2% (4 px)
